question: Unedited and greedy, how often does the model answer each part B task correctly, in the format the runs feed it (raw text; brew: chat with 'Answer:') and in the chat format, whole and hop by hop?
why: Zach (2026-10-19): report Qwen3.5-9B competence on everything; is a smaller model that errs sometimes a better study candidate? (B1 and BREW items, all three formats)

formats.raw: raw text, no chat template, as the part B runs (probe_swap stripped of its trailing space, as exp02's main runs); none for brew
formats.chat: chat template, enable_thinking=False, generation prompt, nothing prefilled. The statement becomes a question after the same context, then ' Answer with a single word and nothing else.' (brew: its own prompt, unchanged; probe_swap: 'Fill in the blank. Answer with only the missing word or words and nothing else.', a blank line, the sentence without 'Fact: ' and ' ___')
formats.chat_prefill: as chat, with the assistant turn prefilled 'Answer:' (brew's format, exp03's render)

kinds.cf: exp09 only: its C prompt (the bridge set to X; answer X's capital or colour), as its eligibility
kinds.off: exp09 only: its O prompt (X's and Z's holders swap; the answer stays)
kinds.hop1: exp09: '<context> <city> is located in' (R, RL) or '<context> <person> lives in' (B, L) -> the bridge (chat: 'In which country is <city> located?' / 'In which country does <person> live?'); brew: 'You stir the potion once.' -> the intermediate. (smoke_v1's wording, '<context> The country where <city> is located is', drew raw continuations such as 'the same as the country where Bob lives' and was replaced)
kinds.hop2: exp09: '<context> The capital of <bridge> is' (R, B) or '<context> <bridge>'s colour is' (L, RL) -> the answer; brew: once, starting from the intermediate -> the answer. probe_swap: no hop prompts

judge.probe_swap: exp13's judge on the continuation: C (the answer as a word sequence in the first clause) and not ambiguous (the swap answer not there too)
judge.others: exp03's answer_colour: the first word of the set in the first non-empty line (capitals: R, B; countries: exp09's hop1; colours: brew, L, RL), equal to the expected answer

generation: greedy, 16 new tokens, prompts of one token length batched 64 at a time (Model.generate_batch, no edits)
reported: per task, format and kind: n, correct, Wilson 95% interval; the first step's probability of the answer's first token (as written, capitalised or lowercase; after a space except at the start of a chat reply); wrong answers by role (the bridge's, X's or Z's, other). exp09: all three of clean, cf and off (its eligibility) and the share of clean-correct items among those with both hops right
reading_aid: a cell is called reliable if its Wilson lower bound is at least 0.85 (a reading aid proposed by the agent, not a decision rule fixed by a human)
baselines: chance among the three in-context options (exp09: 1/3); brew: 1/12 palette colours, or the answer of a one-stir shortcut (the intermediate) and the start, reported as roles
